scenario: AITA for not being emotional on my wedding day? | My wife and I didn’t do many traditional things for our wedding. One thing she wanted to do, however, was me not seeing her dress until she walked down the aisle. I agreed. She kept saying I’d love it, she loved it. She and her best friend (maid of honor) kept sharing reaction posts of grooms happy crying upon getting a first look at their bride, tagging me in it, saying “this will be you!” Day of, wife walks down. She herself did look beautiful, as always. However, I was not big on the dress. To me, it wasn’t at all flattering. But I didn’t focus on that. I focused on her. I smiled. I didn’t break down in tears like some reaction pics/videos. The maid of honor kept nudging me until I looked at her and mouthed “stop”. We got married, kissed, the whole thing. Everything was fine at the reception. Then after our honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend and asked why I had an “underwhelming” reaction to her coming down the aisle. I said I didn’t. She said there are pictures that guests took and I don’t look how she pictured. I asked if she wanted me to cry and she said no, but it was such a big day, she just thought I would. I said I was estatic to marry her and that showed, without me being over dramatic. I also said I had her friend nudging me the whole time and that was unfair to me. Finally I asked if we had a wedding or a play, because I never got lines. Now she’s mad at me. Am I an ass here? I do feel bad she’s disappointed but I couldn’t force myself to have a reaction.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being a "nass" here, which I think is slang for "nervous" or maybe "nervous wreck," but I'm not entirely sure. Anyway, the situation is about my wedding day and how I reacted when my wife walked down the aisle. Let me break this down step by step. First, my wife and I didn't do a lot of traditional wedding things, but she really wanted me not to see her dress until the aisle. I agreed to that. She kept telling me she knew I'd love it, and she loved it too. She and her best friend, who was the maid of honor, kept showing me reaction posts of grooms crying when they see their brides for the first time. They tagged me in it, saying that would be me. So, I guess she had this expectation that I would have a strong emotional reaction, like crying or getting really overwhelmed. On the day of the wedding, my wife walked down the aisle, and she looked beautiful, as always. But honestly, I didn't think the dress was flattering on her. I mean, I didn't focus on that; I focused on her. I smiled, didn't break down into tears like some of those reaction videos. The maid of honor kept nudging me, trying to get me to look at her and mouthed "stop." We got married, kissed, and everything was fine at the reception. After our honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend, and apparently, there were pictures where I didn't look how she pictured. She asked if I wanted me to cry, and I said no, but she was disappointed because it was such a big day, and she thought I would have a stronger reaction. I told her I was ecstatic to marry her, and that showed without being overly dramatic. I also mentioned that the maid of honor was nudging me the whole time, which was unfair. Then I asked if we had a wedding or a play because I never got any lines. Now she's mad at me. I feel bad she's disappointed, but I couldn't force myself to have that reaction. So, am I being a nass here? I don't think so. I was genuine in my reaction. I focused on her, not the dress. I was happy, but I didn't feel the need to cry or overreact. Plus, the maid of honor was pushing me to react, which I found unfair. I think I handled it as best as I could, and maybe my wife is just upset because she had certain expectations that weren't met. I didn't force myself to be emotional, which I think is okay because emotions are personal and shouldn't be forced. I guess the main points are: I was genuine, I focused on my wife, I didn't overreact because that's not who I am, and I didn't appreciate being nudged to react. My wife might be upset because she expected a certain reaction, but I think it's more about her expectations than me being a nass. I handled the situation as I saw fit, and while it's unfortunate she's disappointed, I don't think I did anything wrong.
